Hi Alex — thanks, and great questions. Answers below at a summary level; I attached a short data-flow diagram and our SOC 2 evidence summary for more context. Happy to hop on a quick call if you want line-by-line.

1) Storage & regions- Redwood Hosted API stores customer request payloads, responses, and associated metadata in the cloud region tied to the account’s region selection (US, EU, APAC). For Hightower we observed your account region is US (us-west-2 by default). We do not move production request/response payloads outside the configured region for hosted customers.

2) Default retention & config- By default we retain request/response payloads and token-level traces for 30 days for operational troubleshooting, abuse detection, and model quality monitoring. Audit logs and billing records are retained for 365 days. For enterprise customers we can shorten the payload retention on request (contracted SLAs), and you can elect to have only hashed metadata retained while dropping plaintext inputs/outputs immediately. Dedicated and Private deployments provide stronger guarantees (no hosted logs retained by Redwood beyond customer-configured windows).

3) Deletion process (customer erasure)- Steps we follow once we receive a verified erasure request:
  a) Identify all objects (requests, responses, KV caches, derived artifacts) associated with the tenant ID.
  b) Mark objects for deletion and remove live access within 24 hours.
  c) Purge marked objects from primary object stores within 72 hours.
  d) Removal from backup snapshots occurs at the next backup retention window — typically within 30–35 days. We provide an attestation once the purge cycle completes. Note: for encrypted backups using customer-managed KMS, we can schedule immediate key rotation to render old backups unrecoverable as an option for faster cryptographic erasure.

4) Third-party processors- All hosted API storage and compute are in our cloud accounts; we use managed cloud services (S3, KMS, compute) from major cloud providers. No external vendor accesses plaintext request/response data except for our cloud provider operations under their standard support processes. We also use a managed observability vendor for aggregated telemetry (no request/response payloads). Where needed for audits we share redacted logs or scoped evidence rather than full plaintext.

Alex — answers inline below. I also attached a short playbook with our recommended phrasing (deletion-playbook-steps.txt).

• Backup retention across regions: backup schedule and retention windows are configured per-region but we apply the same retention policy defaults globally. So the 30–35 day cleanup window is consistent across regions unless a customer contract specifies otherwise.

• 30–35 day window detail: the 30–35 day timeframe is the expected maximum for removal from immutable backups following a purge. It reflects the snapshot retention cadence and the time until the next snapshot rotation completes; in contracts we can commit to an upper bound (e.g., 35 days) or implement customer-managed KMS rotation for quicker cryptographic erasure.

• KV caches & batching caches: KV caches used to accelerate model context are short‑lived and are removed as part of the deletion flow. By default KV caches are considered operational ephemeral state and are included in the 30‑day retention window unless you elect a no‑store policy.

Canned paragraph (paste friendly):
"Redwood Inference hosts customer request and response data in the cloud region selected for the customer account (e.g., US, EU, APAC). By default, plaintext request/response payloads and operational caches are retained for 30 days; audit and billing logs are retained for 365 days. Upon a verified data erasure request Redwood removes live data within 72 hours and completes removal from backups within a maximum of 35 days; enterprise customers can request accelerated cryptographic erasure via customer-managed KMS."

Let us know if you want that shortened further.

Regards,
Priya
